description: Strict UE5 content policy for agentic vertical-slice factory. Agents must not directly author or patch Unreal binary assets. Binary content must be produced exclusively by approved Unreal automation from deterministic text sources (specs, manifests, adapters, code).

rules.text_editable: Project-owned source (Source/), config (Config/), future factory roots (specs, manifests, adapters, editor scripts, validators, build scripts), and docs/. Primary targets for Coder and Documentor.
rules.generated_binary: Only inside explicitly assigned paths under coder_generated_output_roots. Must be produced by handoff-approved Unreal Editor automation or commandlet on isolated task worktree. Task branch must own the paths. Must pass Critic audit + map-load/integration verification on candidate.
rules.vendor_content: Marketplace, Fab, sample (e.g. ThirdPerson, Characters/Mannequins), third-party, or vendor roots are read-only. Never modify in place. Integration must use project-owned adapters, manifests, derived assets, or generated content outside vendor roots.
rules.forbidden: Never directly edit or write to Intermediate/, Saved/, DerivedDataCache/, Binaries/, or any transient/generated cache directories. Never synthesize .u* binary files via text edits or direct binary manipulation.
human_gates: Acquiring or purchasing Marketplace/Fab asset packs
Accepting licenses for assets, plugins, or content
Any modification to vendor content roots

enforcement: Enforced via scope_roots.json (readonly_roots, vendor_content_roots, forbidden_roots), Assert-EditScope.ps1, explicit handoff fields (file_ownership + generated_output_ownership), Critic audits of diffs and binary file lists, and candidate integration verification that generated content loads correctly. Assert-BashPolicy.ps1 is listed separately under shell_guard because it is a guard, not an enforcement mechanism.
shell_guard: Assert-BashPolicy.ps1 is a DIRECT-INVOCATION GUARD, not worker containment (scope corrected 2026-07-27; it was wired to nothing at all until that date). It inspects the submitted command string only -- it does not read the body of a script that command runs, nor see processes that script spawns, so one level of script indirection passes it by construction. It catches a careless direct call. Do not plan around it as containment.
